For me, after I'd exhausted all the Douglas Adams material out there (including the highly recommended Dirk Gently books), I moved on to Terry Pratchett (both Discworld and his other stuff, including children's books). Pratchett at his best comes close to Adams' genius but unfortunately he largely substitutes quantity for quality and in latter years seemed to focus too heavily on "what if this thing from our world was in Discworld?" Still, many of his characters (especially Rincewind and Vimes of the Watch) are quite well realized and some of their adventures (especially, imo, the first two books) are very very funny.

Unfortunately, I have never found someone that could approach Adams at his best, lines like

"The ships hung in the sky in much the same way that bricks don't."

have stuck with me since the first time I puzzled over them when I was ten.
